sections.html:
Utah's southwest corner belongs to Washington County, with Arizona to the south and Nevada to the west, across 2,430 square miles. St. George, the county seat since 1856, had 95,342 residents in 2020 and about 106,288 in a 2024 estimate. The county as a whole grew from 138,115 in 2010 to 180,279 in 2020, a rise of 30.5%, and is now near 213,670. In 2020 it had 62,416 households, and about 73.0% were owner-occupied.

Other communities include Santa Clara and Ivins west of St. George, Washington to the east, then Hurricane and La Verkin farther east, plus small places near Zion such as Springdale and Rockville. If you describe your house to anyone valuing it, name the neighborhood, since St. George alone has more than 20 of them, among them Bloomington, Little Valley, Southgate, Sunbrook, The Ledges, Desert Color and Stone Cliff.

Billing and collection sit with the treasurer, while valuation appeals go to the auditor. Both offices are at 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George, UT 84770.

OfficeRolePhone
TreasurerTax notices, payments, delinquent taxes(435) 301-7720
AuditorBoard of Equalization, Tax Commission appeal forms(435) 301-7220
County AdministrationGeneral county contact(435) 301-7000

Real property tax is due November 30 every year, even if no notice reached you. The county mails each owner a notice and sends payment information to the mortgage company, but owners should read the notice for errors. If your neighbors got a notice and you did not, call or email the treasurer for a copy.

The treasurer takes partial payments of $10 or more per parcel at any time. Each payment goes first to interest, then to penalty, then to tax, and when more than one year is delinquent, the most recent year is paid first, as Utah law requires.

There are no payment plans for delinquent taxes. Each May the clerk-auditor sells properties that have been delinquent for at least five years, with a newspaper notice about four weeks beforehand. Utah law does not allow tax liens or tax lien certificates to be sold.

Relief programs run through the clerk-auditor and include exemptions for the blind, a circuit breaker program, and indigent and hardship abatements.

Ask the Board of Equalization to review it. The deadline is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the county auditor gives notice, and the board must rule within 60 days of your application.

A complete application includes your own estimate of fair market value and any evidence that your assessment is out of line with comparable homes. The auditor's appeal page announces when each year's window closes, so check it early in the season and call (435) 301-7220 to confirm.

If you disagree with the board, file Form TC-194 with the county auditor no later than 30 days after the Notice of Determination. The auditor forwards it to the Utah State Tax Commission.

Heat and occasional flooding affect a house here more than anything else. St. George has a mean July daily high of 101.9 degrees, about 60 afternoons a year above 100, and only about 8.8 inches of rain. Monsoon thunderstorms arrive from early July to mid-September, and in January 2005 a flood along the Santa Clara River destroyed 28 homes and killed one person.

Buyers raise two points more than any others: a cooling system near the end of its life, and any house close to a wash or river. Higher country behaves differently, with Pine Valley often getting more than 20 inches of precipitation a year.

Because the tax is a lien on the property, it stays with the house through a change of owner. A mid-year sale means the title company prorates the bill at the closing table, and the settlement statement shows how it was split. Go through it line by line.

  • Find your parcel in the county's tax notice search at outpost.washco.utah.gov.
  • Check whether a lender escrow paid this year's bill.
  • Ask the treasurer to confirm any back balance before closing.
  • Update your mailing address so later notices do not land in an empty house.

sections.h2: If you are behind on taxes
sections.html:
Falling behind is not the end of the road, though the options narrow. A county that offers no payment plan expects the balance in full, and the oldest year does not get paid first: the most recent year does, with each payment applied to interest, then penalty, then tax. Because of that order, a partial payment may not clear a single year's tax right away, so ask the treasurer what a payment will actually cover before you send it.

If the balance is too large to pay and you want to sell, the sale proceeds can pay it at closing. Time matters, because a parcel that stays delinquent for at least five years can be sold in the May sale. Call the treasurer for the amount, then talk to a title company about the closing date.

Three lines deserve a second look: the property tax proration, any payoff to the treasurer and the recording fee. The proration shows each side's share of the year's tax. The payoff line appears only when a balance was open. The deed is recorded with the county, so the statement should show who covers that cost. If a number differs from what the treasurer quoted, ask the title company to explain it before you sign.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited home, rental or vacation house
sections.html:
The situations we hear about most are inherited houses, vacation homes and rentals in St. George and Hurricane. Each has the same checkpoints. Confirm who is on the deed, find out what is owed to the treasurer, and decide whether repairs make sense. Water use and yard condition can matter in a county where most cities limit turf, so a lawn-heavy lot may need a price adjustment.

We buy Washington County houses as-is, which means a buyer who takes the house with its tax balance, its worn cooling system and its dated yard, and pays the balance through closing.

Once you agree to a price, the title company opens the file. It searches the parcel, asks the treasurer for the payoff, and prepares the deed. You sign, the funds are sent, and taxes are divided on the settlement statement. A call to the treasurer at (435) 301-7720 a few days earlier confirms the balance, and the auditor at (435) 301-7220 can answer questions about an appeal that is still open.

faqs.q: When are Washington County, Utah property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 every year, even if you did not receive a notice. Partial payments of $10 or more per parcel are accepted at any time at the treasurer's office, 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Washington County property value?
faqs.a: Apply to the county Board of Equalization by the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor gives notice. Attach your own value estimate and comparable evidence. The auditor at (435) 301-7220 can confirm the filing window for the year.

faqs.q: What if I disagree with the Board of Equalization decision?
faqs.a: File Form TC-194 with the county auditor within 30 days after the Notice of Determination, and the auditor sends it to the Utah State Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Does Washington County sell tax liens?
faqs.a: No. Utah law does not allow tax liens or lien certificates to be sold. The clerk-auditor instead holds a sale each May of properties delinquent at least five years.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Washington County house sells?
faqs.a: The title company prorates it at closing, and your settlement statement shows who pays what. We buy houses as-is here and can work with any tax balance owed.
